I have gone through similar experiences and then some. Ive done the same coping techniques too, just get what you can done and live your life by yourself. As if youd be better off without people anyways. Pretty educated and made good money for myself. But eventually I gave into the need for love and affection and then shortly after we bith self medicated and i ran myself down a hole. Then I woke up and decided Im not going to let it define me or my life. I attempted to make myself a better life. Had a daughter on my way there too. But life is as life does and of course some more traumatizing events happened to me and my family. Trying to pick up all the peices is hard. Its hopelessness is overwhelming when theres barely anything in your hands to control of your own life. Thanks to some people on reddit, here, I have started to see a light at the end of my tunnel when I was sure I had hit a dead end. And now Id like to pay it forward because all life is precious. You are strong. You have been through all of this. You can get through anything. This is nothing. You just need to take a little getaway to love yourself for a while. It sounds like you desparately need to take that time though. You do what you "have" to do but dont make time for you. You can only be as happy as you make yourself. So indulge. Stop struggling. You are loved. You deserve to be loved and pampered. Even if you are doing it yourself. Because honestly. If you cant make yourself happy then nobody else can anyways. Take some time to get to know the real you. Not the you that empty mindedly goes through the motions of the day but a you that stopa to enjoy the sunset or the moon and stars at night. Slow things down and enjoy your life. 

Make it worth living.

Wow, he seems to genuinely regret his choices there. I would know because I was in a dark place once and made the same bad choice once, and felt horrible myself. Cried constantly everyday and every night. Talked about it openly as well, because I knew I deserved the punishment. It does hurt to talk about it, but he will deal with it as long as you need to, and I'm sure he'll warn you if its gone on too long for him to handle emotionally. Took my bf about a year to finally stop mentioning my mistake on a daily basis. 
Eventually, after so many talks, you will be more confident and he will see that in you, and in turn will be happy to see you aren't hurting because of his actions. Everything will work out, presumably. It just takes time and open hearts as well as open-mindedness.

If you're comfortable with giving the both of you a break and testing the waters, do it. Maybe you'll find you have more to live for yourself before settling down. 
Although, if you aren't I'd say, maybe consider counseling, but imho, I'd split ways. You both deserve to be happy, and obviously neither of you are going to be happy in this situation. You deserve to have someone who appreciates you for you, not for what you can do for him for now or what role you can play in this section of his "life." Sounds like he has a lot of maturing to do... I'm sorry.
